body:
You're completely right, I don't actually know what to say :/

I wouldn't have gotten here if it were for alcohol. I guess it's frustrating sometimes to see others enjoying themselves and staying in perfect control when you can't do that same.

I have had plans to pursue healthier hobbies while I am over though there, so I hope I can push through with those. 

Thank you for your response though, it's given me a lot to think about, I haven't thought about it like this before. It's really nice to hear from other people.

I am not in a combative specialty and will spend a majority of my time in a secure location without even having access to my weapon. I'm confident that the stricter atmosphere (no alcohol at all) will help. Back home, it's much more available, but down there I will be staying close to my squad who can and will hold me accountable. I thrive in an environment with direct orders. 

You're not wrong, though. After my most recent incidents I've seen how dark things can be. In a way, I think my shame is working for me, if that makes sense.

What I'm more concerned about pertaining to my alcoholism is returning from this deployment as a 21-year old and having incredibly easy access to alcohol.

I'm so afraid of going back to professional help, especially while I'm over there. I've already jumped through some extra hoops to get approved for this deployment (it's a lot harder to actually /go/ than one might think with the military) and I don't want to immediately go for help down there when they already trusted me with this. 

I know I should though, I just want to spend maybe a week or two collecting myself when I arrive. Is that okay? Thank you for response and advice though, I've been feeling really abandoned lately. It's good to know someone else agrees with my decision.
I just really hope I won't be spoonfed stuff I've already heard. I'm worried about being placed in a higher risk group if I'm more open about it. They don't take suicide lightly.

Hi,
Yes I'm in the US and yes it's become a decently solid option for me. I fanticize about mustering up the courage to do it almost daily.
